# Ingredient assistant evaluation (auto-generated by `python -m src.assistant.evaluate`)

Questions written by the developers, separately from the intent training examples (not a random sample of real users). The development set's first run revealed four general bugs that were then fixed, so its final column is optimistic. The **fresh set** was written after those fixes and its first run is the honest estimate. One later change (an allergen question must name an allergen, found by a unit test) is included in the 'current' column.

| Measure | Dev, first run | Dev, final | **Fresh, first run** | Fresh, current |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Questions | 64 | 64 | 24 | 24 |
| Intent accuracy: keyword rules (baseline) | 67.2% | 67.2% | **83.3%** | 83.3% |
| Intent accuracy: TF-IDF + logistic regression + safety net | 90.6% | 93.8% | **83.3%** | 83.3% |
| Right ingredient found | 96.9% | 96.9% | **100.0%** | 100.0% |
| Answer contains every required fact | 87.5% | 96.9% | **91.7%** | 91.7% |
| Medical questions declined (recall) | 100.0% | 100.0% | **100.0%** | 100.0% |
| Declined answers that were medical (precision) | 100.0% | 100.0% | **100.0%** | 100.0% |
| Follow-up questions ("it" from history) | 80.0% | 80.0% | **50.0%** | 50.0% |

Fresh set: 2 medical and 2 follow-up questions only, so those two rows are small samples.

## Fresh set: failures (2)

Answer correctness per intent: allergens 2/2, contains 1/2, daily_limit 1/1, diet 4/4, list_category 4/4, medical 2/2, portion 1/1, smalltalk 1/1, what_is 4/4, why_added 2/3

* **#102** (Kurkure Masala Munch) “and why is that added” - intent why_added (expected why_added); missing ['anti-caking']. Answer: silicon dioxide (ins 551) is added as carrier. a food additive used to dissolve, dilute, disperse or otherwise physically modify a food additive or nutrient without altering its function (and without exerting any technological effect itself
* **#107** (Coca-Cola) “is there phosphoric acid in coke” - intent why_added (expected contains); missing ['yes']. Answer: phosphoric acid (ins 338) is added as antioxidant, sequestrant. antioxidants are substances which prolong the shelf-life of foods by protecting them against deterioration caused by oxidation, such as fat rancidity and colour changes. seques

## Development set (final): failures (2)

Answer correctness per intent: allergens 8/8, contains 7/7, daily_limit 4/4, diet 9/9, list_category 8/9, medical 8/8, portion 1/1, smalltalk 1/1, what_is 13/13, why_added 3/4

* **#14** (no product) “why do companies add it?” - intent why_added (expected why_added); missing ['acidity regulator']. Answer: citric acid (ins 330) is added as antioxidant, sequestrant. antioxidants are substances which prolong the shelf-life of foods by protecting them against deterioration caused by oxidation, such as fat rancidity and colour changes. sequestran
* **#49** (Amul Butter) “what colour do they add” - intent why_added (expected list_category); missing ['annatto']. Answer: a colour is used because: colours are substances which add or restore colour in a food, and include natural constituents of foods and natural sources which are normally not consumed as foods as such and not normally used as characteristic i

Notes: #102 is a scoring artefact (the answer says “anti caking agent”, the expected phrase was “anti-caking”); it is counted as a failure because the fresh set was not changed after its run. #14 and #102's carrier wording come from the knowledge base itself: Open Food Facts lists citric acid as antioxidant/sequestrant (not acidity regulator) and silicon dioxide as a carrier.
